# Overview

We estimate monthly tuberculosis (TB) **incidence** and the **case-detection
probability** for each of the 27 Brazilian federative units (26 states and the
Federal District) over January 2003 to December 2023 (252 monthly time points per
unit). Both quantities are latent: neither is observed directly. We infer them
from two routinely collected data streams, notifications (SINAN) and deaths
(SIM), linked to incidence through a monthly mechanistic natural-history process.
The model extends the monthly natural-history model of @chitwood2025disruptions,
with the death-reporting adjustment generalised to be time-varying following
@chitwood2021bes. The model is fit one state at a time. These estimates feed a
separate municipality-month panel study of air pollution and TB, so that effects
can be reported on the incidence scale rather than the notification scale.

We do not build a municipality-level incidence model: at municipality-month
resolution TB deaths are too sparse to separate incidence from detection, and a
downscaled outcome would strip the municipality-month variation the panel relies
on. Municipality burden mapping [@chitwood2022spatial] is out of scope here.

## Estimands

For state $s$ and month $t$ we target two quantities:

- $\gamma_{s,t}$: the true incidence rate of symptomatic TB (newly symptomatic
  cases per person-month), reported per 100,000.
- $\delta_{s,t}$: the case-detection probability, the probability that an
  incident case that becomes detectable is notified.

These are kept distinct from the observed notification and death counts
throughout. Observed counts are modelled as realisations of the latent process;
they are never relabelled as incidence.

## The identifying idea

Notifications and deaths are observations generated from incidence through the
natural-history process. They identify incidence and the case-detection
probability **only because informative priors pin the natural-history
parameters** (the survival and case-fatality probabilities and the delay
distributions). The death channel is what identifies detection: for a given
incidence, more deaths imply that fewer cases were detected and treated. Because
this rests on the mortality data, the **death-reporting adjustment is
first-order** and is modelled as time-varying over 2003-2023, since the coverage
and completeness of death registration in SIM improved substantially over the
period. A static adjustment would confound improving registration with falling
incidence and rising detection.

# Data and case definitions

## Notifications (SINAN)

TB notifications are drawn from the Sistema de Informacao de Agravos de
Notificacao (SINAN). The monthly notification count for a state is the number of
records with treatment-entry type "new case" or "relapse" (`TRATAMENTO` codes 1
and 2), excluding re-entry after loss to follow-up, transfer, post-mortem
notification, and unknown entry types. Records are attributed to the
municipality of residence, with the municipality of notification used as a
fallback, and then aggregated to the state. Cases are dated by month of
diagnosis (`DT_DIAG`).

From the same records we derive two state-month covariate series:

- **Treatment-outcome fractions.** The closure-status field (`SITUA_ENCE`) gives,
  among closed cases, the fraction whose outcome is death ($\mathrm{pMort}_{s,t}$)
  and the fraction lost to follow-up ($\mathrm{pAban}_{s,t}$). These enter the
  mortality model as data, not as estimated parameters.
- **Rapid molecular testing (GeneXpert).** The fraction of notified cases with a
  recorded rapid molecular test result (`TEST_MOLEC`), a proxy for diagnostic
  capacity, used as a covariate in the detection sub-model. The roll-out of Xpert
  MTB/RIF in Brazil began around 2014.

## Deaths (SIM)

TB deaths are drawn from the Sistema de Informacao sobre Mortalidade (SIM). A
death is counted as a TB death if its underlying cause is an active-TB ICD-10
code (A15-A19). The monthly state count uses the same residence-with-occurrence
attribution as notifications and is dated by month of death.

From the same all-cause SIM extract we compute the **ill-defined-cause-of-death
(IDC) fraction**: the share of all deaths in a state-month coded to ICD-10
Chapter XVIII (R00-R99, "causas mal definidas"). This series is the covariate
that drives the time-varying death-reporting adjustment.

Using one all-cause extract for both the TB-death count and the IDC fraction
keeps the numerator and denominator on the same attribution rules. State-month
completeness is asserted (every state-year must be present, and no state-month may
have zero all-cause deaths), so a failed or truncated download cannot be silently
treated as zero TB deaths.

## Population (IBGE)

The person-time denominator is the resident population from the Instituto
Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatistica (IBGE), via the SIDRA system. Annual
state-level estimates span the 2000, 2010, and 2022 censuses. We combine the
annual intercensal estimates with the 2022 census count (which revised several
state populations relative to the projections), giving census priority where they
overlap, and interpolate linearly onto monthly mid-points. Population enters the
likelihood as a multiplicative person-time offset, not as a covariate.

# Model

The model is discrete in monthly time and fit separately for each state; the
state subscript is suppressed below. To make the fixed-delay convolutions
complete for the observed window, the latent series are defined on an extended
axis that prepends a pre-window of length equal to the total delay support; only
the observed months enter the likelihood.

## Natural history and likelihood

Let $\lambda_t$ be the per-capita TB infection rate. Incident symptomatic cases
arise by convolving infections with the infection-to-symptom delay,

$$
\gamma_t = \sum_{i\ge 0} \lambda_{t-i}\,\phi^{\lambda}_i ,
$$

where $\phi^{\lambda}$ is the discretised delay kernel. The symptomatic series
$\gamma_t$ is the incidence estimand. Cases become detectable after a second
delay, and a fraction $\delta_t$ of detectable cases are notified:

$$
\text{Notified}_t = \delta_t \sum_{i\ge 0}\gamma_{t-i}\,\phi^{\gamma}_i,
\qquad
\text{Missed}_t = (1-\delta_t)\sum_{i\ge 0}\gamma_{t-i}\,\phi^{\gamma}_i .
$$

Deaths arise on two pathways. Among notified cases, a fraction die during or
after treatment, governed by the observed treatment-outcome fractions and the
conditional probability of death given loss to follow-up. Among missed cases, a
fraction die undiagnosed. Both are spread over the detectable-to-death delay
$\phi^{\text{mort}}$:

$$
\text{AllDeaths}_t = \sum_{i\ge 0}\Big[\text{Notified}_{t-i}\big(\mathrm{pMort}_{t-i}+\mathrm{pAban}_{t-i}\,p_{\text{m}\mid\text{aban}}\big) + \text{Missed}_{t-i}\,p_{\text{m}\mid\text{undx}}\Big]\phi^{\text{mort}}_i .
$$

The two observation channels are Poisson, with the population offset $\text{pop}_t$
converting per-capita rates to expected counts:

$$
\text{SINAN}_t \sim \text{Poisson}\big(\text{pop}_t\,\text{Notified}_t\big),
\qquad
\text{SIM}_t \sim \text{Poisson}\big(\text{pop}_t\,\text{AllDeaths}_t\,\rho_t\big),
$$

where $\rho_t$ is the death-reporting adjustment (@sec-deathadj). Information from
SINAN and SIM about death and loss to follow-up is recorded by notification date,
so the treated-death thinning is applied at the notification month, consistent
with @chitwood2025disruptions.

## Fixed delay distributions

The three delays are fixed (not estimated), taken from @chitwood2025disruptions
and discretised to per-month probability mass functions, truncated at the stated
maxima and renormalised:

| Delay | Distribution | Mean (months) | Max (months) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Infection to symptom onset | Weibull(shape 1.75, scale 25) | 22.3 | 60 |
| Symptom onset to detectable | Gamma(shape 10, rate 4) | 2.5 | 7 |
| Detectable to death | Gamma(shape 12, rate 3) | 4.0 | 10 |

## Latent time structure

Log-incidence and logit-detection are smooth functions of time with three
components, rather than a single log-linear trend with one break. For incidence,

$$
\log \lambda_t = \alpha_{\lambda} + \mathbf{B}_t\boldsymbol{\beta}_{\lambda}
  + \mathbf{S}_t\boldsymbol{\omega}_{\lambda}
  + c^{\text{lev}}_{\lambda}\,\mathrm{COVID}^{\text{lev}}_t
  + c^{\text{slo}}_{\lambda}\,\mathrm{COVID}^{\text{slo}}_t ,
$$

and identically for $\operatorname{logit}\delta_t$ with its own coefficients plus
a GeneXpert term $\beta_x\,\mathrm{Xpert}_t$. Here:

- $\mathbf{B}_t$ is a penalised cubic B-spline basis on coarse (roughly
  annual-to-biannual) knots, capturing the smooth long-run trend. The spline
  coefficients carry a first-order random-walk smoothing prior in a non-centred
  parameterisation.
- $\mathbf{S}_t$ is a Fourier harmonic basis (two harmonics) for the cyclic
  seasonal effect.
- $\mathrm{COVID}^{\text{lev}}_t$ and $\mathrm{COVID}^{\text{slo}}_t$ encode an
  explicit level-and-slope shock from April 2020 onward, modelling the pandemic
  disruption.

We deliberately do **not** include a monthly first-order autoregressive random
walk: it overfit and failed to converge in @chitwood2025disruptions and is
excluded here.

## Time-varying death-reporting adjustment {#sec-deathadj}

@chitwood2025disruptions use a static death-reporting adjustment. Over the full
2003-2023 window we instead model it as a logit-linear function of time and the
ill-defined-cause fraction, following the structure of @chitwood2021bes:

$$
\rho_t = \operatorname{logit}^{-1}\!\big(\theta_0 + \theta_{\text{time}}\,\text{year}_t + \theta_{\text{idc}}\,\mathrm{IDC}_t\big).
$$

This lets improving death registration (a falling IDC fraction and a secular time
trend) be separated from changes in true incidence and detection. The biological
case-fatality parameters are held constant over time; only the reporting
adjustment drifts.

## Priors

The natural-history priors are load bearing and are taken from
@chitwood2025disruptions and @chitwood2021bes:

| Parameter | Meaning | Prior |
|---|---|---|
| $p_{\text{m}\mid\text{undx}}$ | death given undiagnosed | Beta(113, 87), mean 0.565 |
| $p_{\text{m}\mid\text{aban}}$ | death given loss to follow-up | Beta(10, 190), mean 0.05 |
| $\alpha_{\lambda}$, $\boldsymbol{\beta}_{\lambda}$ | incidence level and trend/COVID | Normal(0, 10) |
| $\alpha_{\delta}$, detection coefficients | detection level and trend/COVID | Normal(0, 1) |
| $\theta_0$, $\theta_{\text{idc}}$ | death-adjustment intercept, IDC coef | Normal(0, 1) |
| $\theta_{\text{time}}$ | death-adjustment time trend (per year) | Normal(0, 0.05) |

The fixed-delay kernels and the observed treatment-outcome fractions enter as
data. The incidence intercept is centred at a realistic per-capita log rate to
aid initialisation; this is a numerical centring choice and not an informative
constraint.

# Inference

The model is written in Stan and fit with cmdstanr, one state at a time; a joint
hierarchical fit across all 27 states did not converge in
@chitwood2025disruptions and is not used. Each state is sampled with four chains.
Convergence is assessed with $\hat{R}$ (target $< 1.01$), bulk and tail effective
sample size, and the number of divergent transitions, computed over the
incidence and detection series and all sampled coefficients, not only a few
scalars. We perform a prior predictive check before fitting and a per-state
posterior predictive check against observed notifications and deaths after
fitting. Convergence on the 252-month series is the hardest part; we address it by
reparameterisation (non-centred trend and seasonal terms, informative
initialisation of the per-capita intercept) rather than only raising the sampler
target acceptance.

The implementation is validated by a recovery test: data simulated from the same
generative process with known incidence, detection, COVID, and death-adjustment
parameters are fit, and the model is required to recover the latent series
(interval coverage and correlation) and the signs of the structural terms. An R
implementation of the model's deterministic core is checked to reproduce the
simulator's expected counts exactly, so the simulator and the Stan model are
provably the same data-generating process.

# Reproducibility and software

All data processing is in R with data.table; inference is in Stan via cmdstanr.
The pipeline is a `targets` directed acyclic graph: raw SINAN, SIM, and IBGE
inputs are cached, the state-month panel is assembled, and the 27 per-state fits
run as dynamic branches. Every stochastic step is seeded, including the cmdstanr
fit and the R-side initialisation; paths are relative to the project root; and all
artefacts under `outputs/` are regenerable from code and inputs. Package versions
are pinned with renv and the cmdstan version is recorded with each fit.

# Limitations

TB deaths are defined by underlying cause only, which undercounts deaths where TB
is a contributing cause. The GeneXpert and treatment-outcome covariate
definitions, the exact ill-defined-cause code set, and the population-denominator
reconciliation across the 2010 and 2022 censuses are recorded as decisions
pending confirmation. The death-reporting adjustment is identified from the data
and the IDC covariate but is only weakly anchored to external coverage estimates;
this is the most consequential assumption and is examined in sensitivity
analysis.
